narrative:
**Engagement surged across the board.** Model downloads reached 4,164,974 for the week of 2026-09-14, up 54.9% week over week across a tracked base of 21,458 models, while model likes rose 26.8% to 13,061. Space likes climbed fastest, up 68.8% to 1,315 across 6,222 Spaces. Because only 1-week deltas were available in this pull (4-week and 12-week comparisons were null), it is not possible to say whether this is a sustained inflection or a single-week spike — the magnitude of the download jump in particular warrants a check for ingestion or deduplication artifacts before it is read as organic demand.

**On the model side, the story was share reshuffling among smaller families rather than movement at the top.** Qwen remained the largest classified family at 4,973 models (−3.5%), ahead of Llama at 1,738 (−6.0%) and Gemma at 535 (−3.8%), while the "other-open" bucket grew 4.8% to 5,621. The sharpest gains came from lower-base families: NVIDIA Nemotron rose 415.9% to 227 models, Mistral 115.2% to 213, and Kimi/Moonshot 108.8% to 71, while GLM/Zhipu fell 32.0% to 87 and DeepSeek 6.5% to 187. A key caveat: 7,806 models (36.4% of the 21,458 base) were family-"unknown," so family-level shares are computed on roughly two-thirds coverage and small-family swings may partly reflect improved classification rather than new uploads.

**In Spaces, coding and robotics were the standout use cases.** Coding Spaces rose 33.1% to 233 and its share of all Spaces rose 30.1% to 3.74%; robotics rose 90.7% to 82 Spaces (1.32% share, +86.4%). Chat-assistant remained the largest named category at 974 Spaces (+7.7%, 15.65% share), while education fell 17.6% to 192 and data-analysis fell 8.0% to 474. Within coding, Qwen held a 45.9% family share (up 26.1% relative, n=135); family splits for robotics (n=18), education (n=22), 3D/gaming (n=36) and music (n=42) are too few to report reliably. Technology tags pointed the same direction — quantized +16.6% to 2.19% penetration, multimodal +10.1% to 5.45%, vision-language +6.6% to 7.54% — against declines in long-context (−14.5% to 0.23%) and MoE (−10.4% to 0.71%). Verticals were mixed: enterprise-productivity +12.0% to 7.30% and legal +36.1% to 1.25%, versus education (−14.9%), healthcare (−14.5%) and industrial-manufacturing (−15.0%). SDK mix was stable, with static Spaces up 4.5% to 3,495 and Gradio roughly flat at 2,089 (−0.8%). Next week, watch whether the download and like increases persist against a second comparison point and whether the coding and robotics Space gains hold or revert.
